title: Forgiveness
definition: Forgiveness is the gracious release of personal vengeance and the willingness to extend mercy because God has forgiven sinners in Christ.
summary: Forgiveness flows from the mercy believers have received from God through Christ.
christFocus: Jesus purchased forgiveness through His blood and teaches His people to forgive as they have been forgiven.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Forgiveness is rooted in the Gospel. God forgives sinners through Christ, not by ignoring sin, but by dealing with it at the cross. Believers who have received mercy are called to extend mercy.

Forgiveness does not mean denying harm, excusing evil, or removing all consequences. It means releasing personal vengeance to God and refusing to be ruled by bitterness.

In relationships, forgiveness often opens the way for healing. Reconciliation may require repentance, truth, time, and wisdom, but forgiveness begins with entrusting justice and pain to the Lord.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Bitterness can imprison the heart and continue the damage caused by sin. Forgiveness matters because Christ frees believers from vengeance and teaches them to respond to wrong with Gospel-shaped mercy.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring the offense honestly before God. Ask Him to help you release vengeance, pray for the one who hurt you, and pursue reconciliation where it is wise and biblically possible.
